title: report.json — backtest fixtures report
description: The backtest fixtures report, written to .verdict/backtest/fixtures/report.json and echoed as the `backtest fixtures` envelope's data object: one shape, one schema. It scores recorded reviews against hand-known defects in bench/quality/fixtures.json. Recall is a per-defect hit rate over path + claim, with a mean and a union over N recordings; a union is coverage across runs, not an expected single-run score. Bonus defects are reported separately and never enter recall. Rates describe recorded reviews, not a model claim.

scored.description: Recordings with no infra error, which are the only runs in the recall and false-green denominators.

fixtures.description: One row per fixture, or just the --fixture selection; calibration still covers every archived recording.

calibration.description: The seven archived hand scores, compared as hit-id sets against this build's matcher. reproduced is true only when every row passes; CI checks it, not the rates.

diagnostics.description: Per-recording matcher output: hit ids, praise-only comments, findings with no severity, other findings, the gate outcome and any infra error.

recall.description: per_run is one rate per scored recording; mean is their rounded arithmetic mean; union is the share of known defects any recording hit, with union_hits listing them. A null rate means a zero denominator, never zero recall.

bonus_union.description: Defects listed under bonus that any recording hit. Bonus defects have their own denominator and are never folded into recall.

false_green.description: passes / measured over recordings that reported a gate outcome. gate_passed null is counted in unknown and excluded from measured; a fixture with no measured outcome publishes a null rate.

hallucination.description: S4's quote-verification rate. S6 ships a stub: rate is null, status is stubbed, gating_findings counts the findings the named predicate selects, and checked stays zero. It never reads as a zero hallucination rate.

review_insufficient.description: Exact count of recordings carrying the literal review-insufficient refusal. Other refusal codes, including missing-findings, are not mapped here.

scored.description: False when the recording carries an infra error: its hits are unknown and it is excluded from every rate denominator.
